labels.label: (no ETT label; layer 1) the target's printed form, read against Causal.Causality.stronglyCausal_lift (:332) and alexandrovTopology_eq_lift (:347)
labels.notes: No label exists and none is marked: there is no **`...`** in the file. stronglyCausal_lift has these binders: N M X with topologies; τc : TopologicalSpace N bound before the instance; C, CM, CX; p, D. Its hypotheses are hτ : inst ≤ τc (the coarser topology, see the checks), hC : C.CausallyArcConnected (ADDED), hp/hD (causal curves of ⊤ over [0,1] go to causal curves of ⊤ over [0,1], the weakest reading), hM/hX : StronglyCausal (DEC-7), and hB : HasBasis over every open pair (W, V) with p x ∈ W, D x ∈ V. The conclusion is C.StronglyCausal. alexandrovTopology_eq_lift adds hT : C.Tarentin and concludes C.alexandrovTopology = inst. So the theorems are the target plus exactly one hypothesis, which is disclosed, marked ⚠ strengthened, and recorded with status partial. F1 shows that some such hypothesis is necessary, so the narrower form is the correct certificate, not a finding. 'faithful' here means faithful up to that disclosed addition. The positive theorems are NOT Lean ≥ paper, and no row may treat them as the printed statement.

build.notes: I did not run lake build (per the dispatch). `cd lean-causal && taskset -c 0-11 lake env lean -DwarningAsError=true scaffold/CausalScaffold/StrongCausalityLifts.lean` exits 0 in 3.8 s with no output. grep -w over the file for sorry|admit|axiom|native_decide|sorryAx|implemented_by|extern|unsafe|opaque finds one hit only, the word 'axiom' in the docstring at :744. axioms.txt has 35 entries, one for each #print axioms in Probe.lean, and every one is [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]. checks.F1_refutation: HOLDS. (i) pp.explicit on not_stronglyCausal_lift_of_curves (:647) confirms the binding. C : @Causality N inst, 𝓝 and StronglyCausal use inst, only connectedComponentIn uses τc, and the comparison is inst ≤ τc. So the negated universal is the printed form with the curve hypothesis in its strongest reading: every open U, every open U' ⊇ p(U), every segment. The logic is ¬(∀, H_strong → P), hence ∃ x with H_strong and ¬P, so every reading at least as weak is refuted as well. That covers the [0,1]-at-⊤ reading of the positive theorems, curves over arbitrary intervals (symmRationalLine's curves are locally constant, hence constant on intervals), and any reading in which constant maps are causal curves (DEC-6). (ii) symmRationalLine (:512) is a term of the library's Causality structure (Causal/Causality.lean:55,77), so every axiom is checked by the kernel. I re-checked by hand: le_trans through uIcc_subset_uIcc_union_uIcc, le_mono, and ≪ = ∅ (so le_of_lt and openness are trivial, as for lightlikeLine and rationalLine). (iii) Gluing: symmRationalLine_absolutelyMinimalOn gives ∀ W, AbsolutelyMinimalOn W, the hereditary reading of OQ-95. The M-only reading follows by Precausality.absolutelyMinimal_iff (Causal/Generated.lean:275). M = X = timelikeLine is hereditarily absolutely minimal by CausallyArcConnected.absolutelyMinimalOn_all (Causal/GXStructure.lean:492). My probe proved one statement carrying (∀ W, AbsolutelyMinimalOn W) for N, M and X, Continuous p and Continuous D inside the negated universal, and it compiles. (iv) The causal curves are constant (symmRationalLine_causalCurveOn_eq: IVT plus an irrational value), so id satisfies every reading of 'sends causal curves to causal curves'. (v) J(0,0) ∋ 2, and indeed every rational, so the space is not StronglyCausal (DEC-7). (vi) The basis holds with τc = τ (real_hasBasis_connectedComponentIn_inter), and also with τc = ⊤ indiscrete (real_hasBasis_connectedComponentIn_top_inter), so a strictly coarser τc does not rescue the statement. The witness also meets any implicit hypothesis of the intended setting that bears on maps and spaces: p and D are homeomorphisms (local homeomorphisms, coverings), ℝ is Hausdorff and second countable, and M = X is causal, tarentin and causally arc-connected. It fails only on N: not causal, not tarentin, ≤ not realised by curves.
checks.F1_diagnosis: CORRECT. Causal convexity of S = C(W) ∩ D⁻¹(V) needs, for a, b ∈ S and z ∈ J_N(a,b), both that p z ∈ W and D z ∈ V (monotonicity of p and D at ⊤) and that z lies in the τc-component of p⁻¹(W) through a (a connected set from a to z inside p⁻¹(W)). The author's sentence 'a causal curve with ends in C(W) ∩ D⁻¹(V)' supplies both by putting z on a causal curve from a to b. That presupposes that ≤_M̃ is realised by causal curves. 'Sends causal curves to causal curves' constrains nothing off curves. The witness breaks exactly this step: 2 ∈ J(0,0), yet id is not monotone (2 ≤_N 0 but not 2 ≤ 0 in the timelike line).
checks.F1_minimal_repair: CausallyArcConnected is sufficient but stronger than needed. It asks, for every open U, that ≤_U and ≪_U are both realised by curves of U. The proof uses only harc: ∀ a z, C.le ⊤ a z → ∃ c, C.CausalCurveOn ⊤ c 0 1 ∧ c 0 = a ∧ c 1 = z, that is, ≤ at ⊤ realised by causal curves. harc is the minimal natural repair in the target's vocabulary. My probe proved the target form under harc in place of CausallyArcConnected as a one-line composition of stronglyCausal_of_lift, mem_connectedComponentIn_diamond_of_curves and le_top_map_of_curves, with standard axioms. Weaker still, but not in the target's vocabulary, is the general form's hdiam together with monotone p and D. Under gluing, local causal arc-connectedness also gives harc, through chains of local links and CurveOn.concat (argued, not checked in Lean).
checks.F1_misprint_or_gap: A MISPRINT OF THE HYPOTHESIS (an omitted standing assumption), not a gap in the intended mathematics. In the intended instance the causality of M̃ is ETT's causality from curves (DEC-33), so ≤_U is realised by curves by construction. lean-gx's btzJCLe (GX/BTZ/Topology.lean:1793) is literally the existence of a locally increasing curve in U. gx's def:singular_manifold_endowed_causal is read as Causal.Causality.CausallyArcConnected (lean-gx GX/BTZ/Causality.lean:27). The models are proved arc-connected: GX.E0.causallyArcConnected (GX/BTZ/Causality.lean:1332) and Causal.Model.Massive massive_causallyArcConnected (:187). DEC-147's Lorentzian package also has the causality of curves arc-connected by construction. The abstract statement as printed is still genuinely false, so the F1 finding stands and should go to the author with the amendment. What is still owed in Lean is harc for btzCylCausality / the cover and for Ẽ_α (Q4).
checks.F2: HOLDS (no gluing only, as disclosed). not_alexandrovTopology_eq_lift_of_weakMorphism (:723) negates '∀ …, inst ≤ τc → WeakMorphism p → WeakMorphism D → Tarentin N → SC M → SC X → basis → SC N ∨ Alex N = inst'. Refuting the disjunction refutes both conclusions. The witness timelikeLineTop is in the strict library (Causal/Morphism.lean:708), where it is disclosed as pathological. id is a weak morphism on it, because on every V ≠ ⊤ it is the timelike line. Every diamond at ⊤ is univ, so it is tarentin, not strongly causal, and its Alexandrov topology is the indiscrete one. It is not absolutely minimal (timelikeLineTop_not_absolutelyMinimal), so F2 says nothing under gluing, and the REPORT says so. F2 is a statement about a variant (weak morphisms plus tarentin), not about the printed hypothesis.
checks.positive_theorems: stronglyCausal_lift and alexandrovTopology_eq_lift: the hypotheses are listed in labels[0]. They are the target's plus CausallyArcConnected and nothing else. No continuity, separation or countability is asked. The open form (:360) swaps StronglyCausal for StronglyCausalOpen on M, X and N. The weak-morphism form (:375) is a corollary through the new WeakMorphism.causalCurveOn_comp. The general forms (:220, :249) need neither τ ≤ τc nor curves.
checks.tau_c_direction: CORRECT. In mathlib t₁ ≤ t₂ means t₁ is finer, ⊤ is indiscrete and ⊥ is discrete. hτ : inst ≤ τc therefore says τc is coarser than M̃'s topology. mem_connectedComponentIn_diamond_of_curves uses ContinuousOn.mono_rng hτ (τ-continuous curves are τc-continuous), which typechecks only in this direction. My probe instantiated stronglyCausal_lift with τc := ⊤ and hτ := le_top on the timelike line, and it elaborates, which confirms that 𝓝, C, the curves and StronglyCausal read the instance and only connectedComponentIn reads τc. Intended instance: T_D = natural ∨ D*τ_X in the paper's (coarsest common refinement) sense is mathlib's natural ⊓ induced D τ_X, so hτ is inf_le_left with τc = natural. This matches 'C(W) the component … in the coarser topology'.

checks.antisymmetric_variant: Argued only, and disclosed as such. I checked the argument and it is sound: with φ : ℚ → ℝ hitting every open interval on every open interval, ≤ is antisymmetric and absolutely minimal (choose rational subdivision points with φ increasing), its curves are constant (same IVT argument), and every neighbourhood contains a, b with φ a < φ b whose diamond meets every interval. So making N causal does not rescue the printed form. Not in Lean, so it must not be sent to the author as a theorem.

questions.Q1: SETTLED IN SUBSTANCE: not an open reading. The Lean refutation already decides that some realisation-by-curves hypothesis is needed. The intended instance supplies it by DEC-33 (causality from curves) and by gx's def:singular_manifold_endowed_causal, read as CausallyArcConnected. What goes to the author is the F1 finding and the proposed amended statement, best phrased with harc ('≤ of M̃ realised by causal curves'). The author only confirms the amendment of their own target, so one OQ row (finding plus amendment) is appropriate and it blocks nothing downstream.
questions.Q2: A MATHEMATICAL OPEN PROBLEM, NOT A READING: whether gluing plus weak morphisms makes hdiam unnecessary. It is moot for the intended instances, which are arc-connected. At most it is a planner target. It is not an author ruling. The same open question arises if 'causal map' in the title is read as '≤-monotone map'. The general form already covers that reading, with hdiam.
questions.Q3: SETTLED BY THE CODE. The theorems quantify over every τc with τ ≤ τc (τc = τ included, stronglyCausal_lift_self), and the refutation works with τc = τ and with τc indiscrete. Every reading of 'the coarser topology' is covered. Not an OQ.
questions.Q4: AN OBLIGATION FOR DOWNSTREAM CLOSERS, NOT A QUESTION. The planner should copy it into the evidence of T-loc-btz-tamifying-initial and T-loc-ealpha-tamifying-alexandrov: prove harc (or CausallyArcConnected) for btzCylCausality / the cover and for Ẽ_α. For btzJCLe the curve in the definition, restricted and reparametrised, should be a CausalCurveOn of btzJCausality. Not an OQ.

findings.what: The target-form theorems (stronglyCausal_lift, alexandrovTopology_eq_lift, stronglyCausalOpen_lift, _of_weakMorphism, _self) add C.CausallyArcConnected, but the proof uses only harc (≤ at ⊤ realised by causal curves of ⊤ over [0,1]). kb/0007 and the campaign protocol ask for the weakest sufficient hypotheses. CausallyArcConnected asks for ≤_U and ≪_U realised by curves on every open U, which the instance closers (Q4) would have to prove for nothing. The REPORT discloses this ('uses only the ≤ part at U = M'), so the point concerns the headline statement, not a hidden defect.
findings.fix: Add the target form with harc in place of hC. The auditor's probe proved it as `stronglyCausal_of_lift τc (mem_connectedComponentIn_diamond_of_curves τc hτ harc) (le_top_map_of_curves harc hp) (le_top_map_of_curves harc hD) hM hX hB`, and likewise for the Alexandrov and open forms. Keep the CausallyArcConnected versions as corollaries, and phrase F1's amendment to the author with harc.

findings.what: The claim 'refuted in either reading of gluing' is assembled from several pieces. not_stronglyCausal_lift_of_curves quantifies over gluing-free Causality. N's hereditary absolute minimality is a separate conjunct of symmRationalLine_separates_lift. The gluing of M = X = timelikeLine, which the gluing reading also requires because M and X are ETT causalities too, appears in neither theorem; it is in the library only (CausallyArcConnected.absolutelyMinimalOn_all, Causal/GXStructure.lean:492). The claim is true: the auditor's probe proved the single statement with ∀ W, AbsolutelyMinimalOn W for N, M and X, and Continuous p and Continuous D, inside the negated universal. But what goes to the author should be one checkable declaration.
findings.fix: Add a declaration such as not_stronglyCausal_lift_of_curves_glued carrying (∀ W, C.AbsolutelyMinimalOn W), the same for CM and CX, and Continuous p and Continuous D inside the negated ∀. The probe's proof is the closer's with timelikeLine_causallyArcConnected.absolutelyMinimalOn_all and continuous_id added (import Causal.GXStructure, which is ETT-layer). Optionally add ¬ symmRationalLine.IsCausal and ¬ symmRationalLine.Tarentin to symmRationalLine_separates_lift. Both are true but are stated only in prose at :65-66 and in the REPORT.

findings.what: The basis hypothesis is read as HasBasis over every open pair (W, V). That reading is literal, and it makes each C(W) ∩ D⁻¹(V) a neighbourhood. The positive proofs use this through hB.mem_of_mem on arbitrary pairs (:239, :211). A weaker reading, 'x̃ has a neighbourhood basis consisting of some sets of this form', is not discussed, and under it the proof's neighbourhood step is not available. The refutation is unaffected, since the witness meets the stronger reading. In the intended instance the two coincide (τc locally connected, p τc-continuous).
findings.fix: One sentence in the readings/SCOPE saying the index ranges over all open W ∋ p x̃ and V ∋ D x̃, and that a sub-family reading would need each C(W) ∩ D⁻¹(V) to be a neighbourhood, which holds in the intended instance.
